chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Term Sheet as a Document

lessons.title: Term Sheet Basics: Binding vs Non-Binding Clauses

children.text: Rohan has just moved ₹20 lakh into a separate savings account, ready to invest in ChaiCart's Series A round. ChaiCart's founder, Ananya, emails him a two-page PDF titled "Term Sheet, Non-Binding" and asks him to sign and return it by Friday. Rohan reads the words "non-binding" and relaxes. He should not relax completely. A term sheet is not a contract to buy shares, but parts of it can bind him the moment he signs.

body.text: A term sheet is a map of the deal, not the deed to it. Most of it, including valuation and liquidation preference, can still be renegotiated or walked away from. A handful of clauses, usually confidentiality, exclusivity and governing law, bind you the day you sign, whatever the header says.

children.text: What a Term Sheet Actually Is
A
term sheet

is a short document, usually two to six pages, that records the commercial terms both sides have provisionally agreed to before lawyers draft the real contracts. In an Indian angel round it typically covers the investment amount, the instrument being issued, valuation, price per share, and a short list of investor rights such as board representation, information rights and anti-dilution protection. None of this is final. It is a starting point for drafting, not a substitute for it.

markDefs.definition: A short, mostly non-binding document setting out the commercial terms of an investment before lawyers draft the legally binding agreements.

children.text: Three names get used almost interchangeably in Indian deals: term sheet, letter of intent (LOI), and heads of terms. All three mean the same thing: a statement of intent to invest, subject to conditions, that is not itself a purchase of shares.
The Legal Chain: From Term Sheet to Money in the Bank
Signing a term sheet does not move a single rupee. It starts a sequence that, for a straightforward Indian angel round, usually takes four to eight weeks.

body.title: From Signed Term Sheet to Allotted Shares

events.title: Term Sheet Signed
events.description: Ananya and Rohan sign. Commercial terms are provisionally locked, but nothing is legally final yet.

events.title: Due Diligence and Drafting
events.description: Rohan reviews ChaiCart's financials, cap table and material contracts. Lawyers draft the Share Subscription Agreement (SSA) and Shareholders' Agreement (SHA).

events.title: Exclusivity Window Closes
events.description: The no-shop clause in the term sheet typically locks ChaiCart out of talking to other investors for 30 to 45 days from signing.

events.title: Board and Shareholder Approvals
events.description: ChaiCart's board and existing shareholders pass the resolutions needed to issue fresh CCPS under Sections 42 and 62 of the Companies Act, 2013.

events.title: Definitive Agreements Signed
events.description: Rohan signs the SSA and SHA. The Articles of Association are amended to include CCPS rights.

events.title: Funds Transferred and Shares Allotted
events.description: Rohan wires ₹20 lakh. ChaiCart allots the CCPS and must file Form PAS-3 with the Registrar of Companies within 15 days of allotment.

children.text: Notice what the term sheet does not do: it does not transfer money, issue shares or amend the Articles. Those happen later, through the
definitive agreements

, namely the SSA, the SHA and the amended AoA. If the term sheet and the definitive agreements ever disagree, the definitive agreements win. Most SSAs contain an "entire agreement" clause that says exactly this.

markDefs.definition: The legally binding contracts that replace a term sheet once negotiation is complete: typically the Share Subscription Agreement (SSA), the Shareholders' Agreement (SHA), and the amended Articles of Association (AoA).

children.text: Binding on Paper, Binding in Practice

Every Indian term sheet is headed something like "This Term Sheet is not intended to be legally binding, save for Clauses X, Y and Z." That carve-out list matters more than the header itself. In practice, three kinds of clauses almost always survive as binding, whatever the rest of the document says.

body.caption: What usually survives as binding, whatever the header says

cells: Stops either side sharing deal terms, financials or the fact that talks are happening
Protects sensitive information exchanged during diligence, whether or not the deal closes
Stops the company from soliciting or accepting a competing offer for a fixed period
Gives the investor a clear window to finish diligence without being outbid mid-process
Fixes which country's law applies and how disputes get resolved, in courts or by arbitration
Needs to apply to any dispute about the term sheet itself, including its non-binding terms
States who pays legal and due diligence costs if the deal falls through
Allocates a real, immediate cost that cannot wait for definitive documents

body.title: What stays negotiable vs what is locked in, once signed

columns.label: Binding: locked in from signing
points: Governing law and dispute resolution forum
Allocation of diligence and legal costs

body.text: For a small angel cheque, exclusivity usually protects the investor, not the founder. It stops ChaiCart from shopping the deal to a better-funded investor while Rohan is still doing diligence. If Rohan is the one who gets cold feet, exclusivity does nothing to force him to invest. Nobody can be forced to sign definitive agreements just because they signed a term sheet.

children.text: Rohan's Term Sheet From ChaiCart
ChaiCart is raising the same ₹1 crore Series A at a pre-money valuation of ₹4 crore and a price of ₹3,200 per share. Rohan's ticket is ₹20 lakh, which buys him 625
Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares (CCPS)
. The remaining ₹80 lakh, 2,500 CCPS, comes from two other angels in the same round.

markDefs.definition: Preference shares that must convert into equity shares by a fixed date or trigger event. CCPS is the standard instrument issued to institutional and larger angel investors in priced Indian startup rounds.

body.title: Show me the actual clause language

children.text: Clause 14, Binding Effect
(illustrative wording):

"This Term Sheet does not create a binding obligation on either party to consummate the Proposed Transaction, save that Clauses 9 (Confidentiality), 10 (Exclusivity) and 15 (Governing Law) shall be binding on the parties from the date of execution."
Clause 10, Exclusivity
(illustrative wording):

"For a period of 45 days from the date of this Term Sheet, the Company shall not, and shall procure that its directors and shareholders do not, solicit, negotiate or accept any offer of investment from any third party."

Notice the structure: one clause lists exactly which numbered clauses are binding. Always check that carve-out list line by line before you sign, since founders sometimes reuse a template from an earlier round and forget to update the clause numbers.

body.label: Not every early-stage deal uses a term sheet
body.context: 100X.VC's iSAFE (India SAFE), used in many Indian pre-seed rounds, is a standardised convertible instrument with pre-agreed terms. Investors sign the iSAFE directly, without a separate negotiated term sheet stage.

body.title: Exclusivity Breach
body.scenario: Twenty days into the 45-day exclusivity period, Rohan hears from a common friend that Ananya has been in active conversations with a larger fund about a bigger cheque at a better valuation for ChaiCart. Rohan has already spent ₹40,000 on a chartered accountant for diligence.
body.prompt: Is Ananya doing anything wrong, and what can Rohan realistically do about it?
body.modelAnswer: Yes, if this term sheet's Clause 10 carves out exclusivity as binding, ChaiCart is not permitted to negotiate with another investor during the 45-day window, whatever the rest of the document says. Rohan's realistic options at this ticket size are limited: ask Ananya directly to confirm in writing whether talks are happening; if confirmed, treat it as a breach and decide whether to walk away and seek reimbursement of the ₹40,000 diligence cost, since a well-drafted term sheet often makes the company bear costs on a breach it caused; and recognise that suing a founder for specific performance to force the round through is almost never worth it on a ₹20 lakh cheque. In practice, angels protect themselves less through litigation and more by moving quickly during the exclusivity window and by choosing founders carefully before signing anything.

body.title: What Actually Binds ChaiCart
body.question: Rohan's term sheet says it is non-binding, except for Clauses 9, 10 and 15 (Confidentiality, Exclusivity and Governing Law). Which of the following can ChaiCart still walk away from without breaching the term sheet?
options: The agreed pre-money valuation of ₹4 crore
The 45-day restriction on talking to other investors
The choice of Indian courts or arbitration for disputes
body.explanation: Valuation is a commercial term, and commercial terms are non-binding by default unless specifically carved out. Confidentiality, exclusivity and governing law are the three clauses carved out as binding in this example, so ChaiCart cannot ignore them, but the ₹4 crore pre-money figure can still move if renegotiation happens before the SSA and SHA are signed.

stats.context: Common range in Indian angel and seed term sheets

children.text: Why Bother With a Term Sheet at All

If most of it is non-binding, why sign anything before the real contracts? Three reasons. Cost: a term sheet is one or two pages that a founder and investor can negotiate themselves in days, while an SSA and SHA can run to 40 or 50 pages and need lawyers on both sides, so nobody wants to pay for that drafting until the big commercial terms are settled. Speed: once signed, the exclusivity clause gives the investor a clear runway to finish diligence without a bidding war breaking out underneath them. Signal: for a founder juggling several conversations, a signed term sheet is the clearest proof available that a particular investor is serious, well before any money changes hands.
Two more phrases turn up in almost every term sheet.
Conditions precedent
are the boxes that must be ticked before the deal can close, typically clean due diligence, board approval, and no material adverse change in the business. The
long-stop date

is the deadline by which those boxes must be ticked. Miss it, and either side can walk away without penalty. Neither term matters until an actual round is being negotiated, which is exactly what this course covers.

markDefs.definition: Conditions that must be satisfied before an investment can close, such as clean due diligence, required approvals, and no material adverse change in the business.
The deadline by which all conditions precedent must be met and definitive agreements signed. After this date, either party can typically walk away without penalty.

body.title: The Default Rule
body.textWithBlank: Unless a term sheet clause is specifically carved out as binding, such as confidentiality or exclusivity, its commercial terms like valuation and liquidation preference are treated as ___.
body.explanation: Indian market practice, stated explicitly in almost every term sheet, treats commercial terms as non-binding and open to renegotiation until the definitive agreements, the SSA, the SHA and the amended AoA, are actually signed.

body.label: MCA: Ministry of Corporate Affairs
body.description: Search company filings and find e-Form PAS-3 (Return of Allotment) and other statutory forms a company must file once a term sheet turns into an actual share allotment.

cards.definition: A short, mostly non-binding document recording the commercial terms of an investment before the definitive legal agreements are drafted.
The default status of a term sheet's commercial terms, such as valuation and liquidation preference, meaning either party can walk away or renegotiate without breaching it.
A binding clause stopping the company from soliciting or accepting competing investment offers for a fixed period, typically 30 to 45 days in Indian rounds.
A binding clause preventing either party from disclosing deal terms or information shared during diligence.
Conditions that must be satisfied, such as clean diligence or board approval, before the investment can close.
The legally binding contracts that replace the term sheet: the Share Subscription Agreement (SSA), the Shareholders' Agreement (SHA), and the amended Articles of Association.
The deadline by which the deal must close or either party can walk away without penalty.

points: A term sheet records commercial terms provisionally. It does not transfer money, issue shares or amend the Articles.
Most of its content, including valuation, liquidation preference and board rights, is non-binding by default and can still change before definitive agreements are signed.
Confidentiality, exclusivity/no-shop and governing law clauses are typically carved out as binding from the date of signing, whatever the document's header says.
Exclusivity generally protects the investor by stopping the company from shopping the deal elsewhere during diligence. It rarely forces the investor to complete.
The term sheet is superseded by definitive agreements: the SSA, the SHA and the amended Articles of Association.
Conditions precedent and a long-stop date set the finish line and the deadline for turning a signed term sheet into an actual, funded investment.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not legal or investment advice. ChaiCart and Rohan are fictional and used for illustration, and the clause language shown is illustrative rather than a template for a real transaction. Term sheet drafting varies by deal and should always be reviewed by a qualified lawyer before signing. Startup investments are high risk, illiquid, and can result in the loss of your entire capital.
